classifications.source_derived: value taken from a normative source (R1/R2) with its locator
classifications.source_scale_adapted: normative scale or convention adapted to the one-NGS SCAO topology or to this repository's frame semantics; the adaptation is stated
classifications.engineering_assumption: value no source supplies, chosen for a stated engineering reason and not tuned to a literature Strehl
classifications.declared_experiment_choice: a choice that defines the experiment (tier size, science wavelength, weak gate atmosphere), declared before running
classifications.software_policy: a software convention with no physical content

rows.title: Primary diameter
rows.rationale: historical E-ELT DRM primary
rows.limitation: the current ELT is 39 m; this is the historical DRM design

rows.title: Central-obstruction diameter ratio
rows.rationale: annular pupil, area pi/4 D^2 (1 - 0.28^2)
rows.limitation: applied unchanged to the 5 m and 12 m tiers, whose obstruction is therefore a declared tier choice rather than a source value

rows.title: Segmentation and spiders omitted
rows.rationale: first reference case is the pure annulus
rows.limitation: no segment piston, gap diffraction or spider island effects

rows.title: Integrated Fried parameter
rows.rationale: packaged literature profile literature_profiles/eso_elt_drm_ten_layer.json
rows.limitation: zenith profile; seeing 0.8 arcsec is the rounded Kolmogorov value

rows.title: Outer scale and absolute normalization
rows.rationale: absolutely normalized von Karman layers, no RMS rescaling; block-level wind is zero because each layer carries its own
rows.transformation: periodic FFT band (2x pupil) plus analytic low-frequency quadrature (layered_atmosphere.py)
rows.limitation: the periodic band repeats after one screen period of travel; reported per run

rows.title: Ten layers: altitudes, Cn2 fractions, wind speeds
rows.rationale: verbatim packaged table
rows.transformation: fractions divided by their printed sum 1.001 (normalized sum exactly 1)
rows.limitation: altitudes are recorded but unused on axis

rows.title: 84x84 SH and 85x85 ground DM
rows.rationale: the R1 high-order scale
rows.transformation: borrowed into a one-NGS, on-axis SCAO topology (A01)
rows.limitation: R1 used these scales in LGS/MCAO-type studies; nominal square-grid counts, not active counts

rows.title: Loop rate
rows.rationale: R1 500 Hz
rows.limitation: none

rows.title: Reference run length
rows.rationale: the long reference run
rows.transformation: science exposure excludes the declared burn-in (A11)
rows.limitation: the full-scale capability tier overrides this to 20 frames, which is not a converged performance result

rows.title: Delayed command: three iteration intervals
rows.rationale: the canonical loop already contributes one frame (frame k's update is first seen at frame k+1), so a total measured-to-applied delay of three intervals is latency_frames = 2
rows.limitation: no fractional delay and no finite-exposure integration (A10)

rows.title: Deterministic noiseless sensing
rows.rationale: R1 idealized-noise limit adapted to the one-NGS case
rows.transformation: no photon, read, dark or background noise in calibration or loop
rows.limitation: no noise propagation or aliasing-with-noise term; not R3's 3 e- or R4's photon budget

rows.title: One on-axis natural guide star
rows.rationale: SCAO topology: one NGS at infinity on axis; no off-axis propagation, cone effect or finite source range
rows.transformation: layer altitudes are recorded but have no effect on axis
rows.limitation: no anisoplanatism, no LGS

rows.title: Wind azimuths
rows.rationale: R1 publishes no directions; every layer toward +x as in the other packaged profiles; on-axis SCAO statistics depend on speeds
rows.limitation: a common direction is a worst case for temporal correlation of layers

rows.title: WFS wavelength
rows.rationale: monochromatic 700 nm sensing, the repository's existing convention; inside R3's 0.6-0.9 um band but not a claim about any published bandpass
rows.limitation: monochromatic sensing, no chromatic effects

rows.title: Science wavelengths
rows.rationale: the required 2.2 um monochromatic example; the smoke tier adds 1.65 um to exercise multi-wavelength accumulation
rows.limitation: monochromatic images only; no broadband coaddition

rows.title: Pupil raster
rows.rationale: 12 pupil samples per lenslet in every tier (pixel spacing D/(N-1) = 41.7 mm at full scale); lenslet edges then coincide with actuator rows
rows.transformation: samples span the diameter end to end (build_pupil_geometry)
rows.limitation: sampling convergence must be checked (ESO-08); 1024 samples is supported without rounding

rows.title: Atmospheric high-frequency cutoff
rows.rationale: carries forward the packaged atmosphere's convention: no power above the pupil grid's Nyquist frequency (R1 'inner scale = pixel size')
rows.limitation: sub-pixel turbulence is absent; the per-lenslet sampling (12 samples) bounds intra-subaperture structure

rows.title: SH focal sampling and detector window
rows.rationale: pad 2 gives Nyquist sampling (pixel lambda/(2d) = 0.144 arcsec at 700 nm, d = 0.5 m) on a 24-pixel FFT canvas; the detector window is the 23 pixels symmetric about the optical-axis pixel, so a centre of gravity of a symmetric spot reads exactly zero (revision 1 -> 2)
rows.transformation: pupil samples per lenslet (12) and detector pixels per spot canvas (24, window 23) are separate quantities; one canvas row and column is outside the window
rows.limitation: no field stop or spatial filter; canvas periodicity aliases far spot wings; the trimmed row/column is reported as window clipping; not R1's '6' CCD sampling

rows.title: Lenslet illumination threshold
rows.rationale: retain lenslets at least half illuminated; partial edge lenslets above the cut keep their real partial masks
rows.limitation: a different cut changes the retained count and edge correction

rows.title: Centroiding and validity policy
rows.rationale: plain center of gravity over the whole canvas; validity thresholds as in the repository's detector profiles, which noiseless sensing at the A09 scale passes
rows.limitation: thresholds are engineering values; usable fractions are reported, never relaxed to close the loop

rows.title: Lenslet vertex convention of a schema-v8 record
rows.rationale: a record of schema v6 or later states where the microlens vertices sit; the value is the one every earlier record of these tiers ran with, so the sensor is unchanged
rows.limitation: read by the HCIPy optics backend only; the native backend of these tiers does not use it

rows.title: Linear-spline basis
rows.rationale: R1 names a linear-spline family; implemented as the separable bilinear tent w = L((x-xi)/p) L((y-yi)/p), L(t) = max(0, 1-|t|), support one pitch, unit value at the actuator centre with no sampled renormalization (partition of unity)
rows.transformation: sampled at pupil-sample centres, zero outside the pupil
rows.limitation: a declared interpretation, not a proven ESO implementation; not the radial pyramid_like family

rows.title: Actuator pitch and alignment
rows.rationale: actuators at linspace(-D/2, D/2, N): pitch D/(N-1) equals the lenslet pitch and actuators sit on lenslet corners (Fried geometry)
rows.limitation: no misregistration

rows.title: Retained physical actuator layout
rows.rationale: retain every nominal actuator whose support square can reach the pupil disk (centre radius <= R + sqrt(2) p); physical IDs keep their nominal grid indices
rows.limitation: retained counts are reported separately from illuminated and calibrated counts

rows.title: Zero-support exclusion and controlled subset
rows.rationale: actuators with no illuminated support (central obstruction, outside the disk) or no retained-lenslet support stay in the layout and are excluded with their reason; every other actuator is calibrated and solved
rows.transformation: controlled-subset projection back to the full layout
rows.limitation: no hardware faults in the reference case

rows.title: No physical camera block
rows.rationale: a record of schema v7 or later states whether the physical camera path is selected; these tiers keep the ideal detector of version 2
rows.limitation: no detector-pixel layout, photometric budget or calibration products

rows.title: Integrator gain and leak
rows.rationale: a pure integrator with a gain inside the stability region of a three-interval delay; not optimized against Strehl
rows.limitation: no modal gain optimization, no predictive control

rows.title: Reconstruction objective
rows.rationale: Tikhonov least squares on the usable rows starts from zero. The profile factor of 0.001 times the RMS response column norm suppresses unseen piston and waffle combinations while leaving the lowest seen modes essentially undamped. Version 3 uses 0.03 as a common engineering setting for 5 m and 12 m. At 5 m this setting improved on 0.001 and gave 103 +- 19 nm2 more total variance than the lowest measured mean, at 0.07. At 12 m the lowest noiseless sample mean was at 0.03. The 42 m tier retains 0.001.
rows.limitation: not a turbulence-prior MMSE estimator

rows.title: Calibration probes
rows.rationale: 20 nm OPD central differences of every eligible actuator, grouped so no two probes share a lenslet
rows.transformation: grouping is exact for local optics and noiseless sensing
rows.limitation: linearity checked at 5-40 nm; noise-on scalable calibration is refused

rows.title: Waffle-family filter
rows.rationale: every reconstructed increment loses its projection on the calibrated response's weakly sensed checkerboard family (commands that are mostly local waffle and are sensed below 0.35 of the RMS response column norm); the relative damping of row A07b does not regularize that family, and the closed loop accumulates aliased turbulence in it (revision 2 -> 3); version 4 of the 12 m tier uses 0.6, the lowest sample mean of eleven tested cutoffs at that aperture, where the family has 20 modes and at 0.35 it has 11 (revision 3 -> 4)
rows.transformation: family from shwfs_ao.calibration.sparse.response_waffle_modes at the effective cutoff of each profile: 0.35 for the version-3 profiles and 0.6 for eso_scao_medium_12m_derived@4; projection removed after the LSMR solve
rows.limitation: 0.35 at 5 m and 42 m is the value of det_ccd_42m_r3band_derived@2; the cutoff was scanned at 5 m and 12 m and not at 42 m; tested with noise at 12 m only

rows.title: Stroke semantics
rows.rationale: a finite engineering limit (100 um OPD) standing in for an unbounded DM; every run reports its measured saturation fraction, which must be exactly zero for the approximation to hold
rows.limitation: infinity is not encoded; a run with any saturation is not an unbounded-stroke result

rows.title: Numerical electron scale
rows.rationale: a numerical scale for the noiseless image-based SH; normalized slopes are invariant to it within the validity range; not a measured guide-star flux
rows.limitation: it sets validity diagnostics (flux, SNR proxies), not noise

rows.title: Timing model
rows.rationale: frame k is one instantaneous atmosphere sample at k/500 Hz; detector.exposure_s = 1/f is recorded, not integrated; frame k's increment is released in the update of frame k + latency_frames and first seen at frame k + 3; science uses the pre-update residual
rows.transformation: rectangle-rule temporal quadrature of instantaneous snapshots
rows.limitation: no finite-exposure WFS integration, no fractional latency, no DM settling

rows.title: Science selection, grid and metrics
rows.rationale: burn-in per tier (ci 8, medium 50, medium-gate 30, full 5, reference 200 frames), stride 1, equal weights, pre-update residual; pad 2 gives lambda/(2D) pixels over the full uncropped FFT grid; Strehl = final-image peak / ideal peak; FWHM, EE and radial profile about the final-image peak; flux denominator = normalized source grid
rows.transformation: intensity averaging of instantaneous images, no recentring
rows.limitation: burn-in is set before inspecting results; the 20-frame full tier is not a settled long exposure

rows.title: Numerical settings that can change results
rows.rationale: LSMR from x0 = 0 to 1e-8 relative tolerances agrees with a direct Tikhonov solve to ~1e-8 on an 84x84 Fried operator in ~270 iterations; a non-converged solve is rejected; float64 throughout; lenslet batch size and thread counts are execution settings outside the identity
rows.limitation: solver tolerance enters the command at the 1e-8 relative level

rows.title: Lower-order tier geometry and lengths
rows.rationale: distinct lower-order experiments that keep the full tier's 0.5 m pitch and 12 samples per lenslet; the smoke tier is a software-smoke label
rows.limitation: not rescaled ESO results; changing aperture at fixed pitch changes the physical experiment

rows.title: Predeclared weak atmosphere for the control gate
rows.rationale: r0 = 0.40 m at 500 nm, declared before any gate run; layers, L0 and winds are the R1 ones
rows.limitation: an engineering gate, not an ESO condition

rows.title: Software conventions
rows.rationale: native NumPy backend; the root seed is a declared reproducibility input
rows.limitation: other realizations use realization_index

revisions.reason: The whole 24-pixel Nyquist canvas has one more row and column on the negative side of the optical-axis pixel. A centre of gravity over it reads a negative slope for symmetric spots that broaden (measured -0.005 px for a symmetric local defocus), and the closed loop settles on a compensating static tilt: +2.6e-8 rad in x and +1.8e-8 rad in y on the 5 m tier, and the one-pixel (+0.5, +0.5) lambda/D offset of the 42 m long exposure (peak Strehl 0.78, on-axis 0.20). A 23-pixel window is symmetric about the axis pixel: zero bias for symmetric spots, closed-loop tilt within atmospheric wander.
revisions.not_tuned_to: no Strehl target; the criterion is a zero centroid for symmetric spots

revisions.change: reconstructor.waffle_filter_cutoff absent -> 0.35 for version 3 of the 5 m, 12 m and 42 m tiers
revisions.reason: In the noiseless production closed loop the residual wavefront RMS falls from 191.98 +- 1.40 to 173.53 +- 0.90 nm at 5 m (five realizations of 2000 frames), from 183.16 +- 2.02 to 172.10 +- 1.51 nm at 12 m (five realizations of 1000 frames) and from 173.65 to 167.17 nm at 42 m (one realization of 1000 frames; three filtered realizations give 168.06 +- 0.65 nm).
evidence: outputs/tiptop_native_comparison/2026-11-10/e4_ensemble (five realizations at 5 m and 12 m, one at 42 m, with and without the filter; not tracked)
outputs/tiptop_native_comparison/2026-11-10/e22_alpha_scan (Tikhonov-factor scan at 5, 12 and 42 m, and three 42 m realizations; not tracked)
revisions.not_tuned_to: no Strehl target and no value of the Fourier model; the cutoff is the one already published for det_ccd_42m_r3band_derived@2

revisions.change: reconstructor.alpha 0.001 -> 0.03 for version 3 of the 5 m and 12 m tiers
revisions.reason: With the filter on, 0.05 and 0.07 reduced 5 m total variance by about 400 nm2 relative to 0.001 on five paired realizations. The common factor of 0.03 reduced it by 302.2 +- 20.5 nm2, and 0.15 raised it. At 12 m the production image sensor and reconstructor in the test-side loop gave 431 +- 26 nm2 less in-DM-space variance at 0.03 on twelve noiseless realizations. In the four-realization production loop, 0.03 reduced total variance by 348 +- 43 and 356 +- 78 nm2 at 1000 and 500 photons with 1 e- read noise. The lowest sample mean was at 0.03 without noise and at 1000 photons, and at 0.02 at 500 photons, where 0.03 was 16 +- 51 nm2 higher. A common optimum or equal gain across noise conditions remains unestablished. At 42 m only 0.001 and 0.03 had three paired realizations. Their change from 0.001 to 0.03 was +44 +- 42 nm2, leaving the 42 m optimum open.
evidence: outputs/tiptop_native_comparison/2026-11-10/e4_ensemble (five realizations at 5 m and 12 m, one at 42 m, with and without the filter; not tracked)
outputs/tiptop_native_comparison/2026-11-10/e22_alpha_scan (Tikhonov-factor scan at 5, 12 and 42 m, and three 42 m realizations; not tracked)
revisions.not_tuned_to: no Strehl target and no value of the Fourier model; the criterion is the closed-loop residual variance on paired atmospheres, and one value is used for the two tiers where it helps

revisions.change: wfs.lenslet_axis and detector_physics stated for the schema-v8 records
revisions.reason: The filter field exists only in schema v8, whose records must state two fields that schema v5 omits. Both take the values version 2 ran with.

revisions.change: reconstructor.waffle_filter_cutoff 0.35 -> 0.6 for version 4 of the 12 m tier
revisions.reason: At a Tikhonov factor of 0.03 on five paired noiseless realizations of the 12 m production closed loop, cutoff 0.6 gave the lowest sample mean of eleven tested cutoffs: 419 +- 42 nm2 of total variance below 0.35, 68 +- 10 nm2 below 0.5 and 36 +- 9 nm2 below 0.7, with 0.9 and 1.0 above 0.35. With 1 e- of read noise on four realizations it was 406 +- 79 nm2 below 0.35 at 1000 photons and 355 +- 60 nm2 below at 500 photons. At cutoffs 0.5 and 0.7 a factor of 0.03 gave the lowest sample mean of five tested factors. At 5 m, 0.35 gave the lowest sample mean of six tested cutoffs and cutoffs of 0.5 and above raised the variance by 226 +- 45 nm2 or more, so that tier keeps 0.35. The cutoff was not scanned at 42 m.
evidence: outputs/tiptop_native_comparison/2026-11-10/e23_waffle_cutoff_scan (cutoff scan at 5 m and 12 m at a factor of 0.03; not tracked)
outputs/tiptop_native_comparison/2026-11-10/e24_k12_cutoff_followup (more cutoffs, the factor at cutoffs 0.5 and 0.7, and read noise at 12 m; not tracked)
revisions.not_tuned_to: no Strehl target and no value of the Fourier model; the criterion is the closed-loop residual variance on paired atmospheres
